full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued granting leave to revision to the petitioners calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 9-11-2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.196 of 2013 disallowing the revision and thereby affirming the order dated 22-9-2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in House Rent Case No.6 of 2005 rejecting an application filed by the petitioner under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying permission to withdraw/take back the deposited amount as house rent should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner filed House Rent Case No.6 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court and House Rent Controller, Dhaka for depositing the monthly rent for the suit premises stating, inter alia, that the petitioner entered into an agreement with the opposite parties on 1-2-1982 for lease of a room being No.2B in the 1st Floor of Holding No.1/1, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka by fixing the monthly rent at Taka 1,200, which was subsequently renewed from time to time and lastly on 1-1-2002 and monthly rent was also increased from time to time on mutual consent. The petitioner made payment of monthly rent to the opposite parties who issued receipts for the same. On 21-11-2004 at about 9-00 pm a fire accident took place in the Gulistan 'Hawker Market' which spreaded out to the adjacent building including the case premises and completely burnt the market causing loss to the petitioner to the tune of taka one crore for which the petitioner lodged a general diary with the Motijheel Police Station on 23-11-2004. Due to the fire accident the petitioner became looser even then she offered monthly rent to the opposite party for the month of November, 2004 on 5-12-2004 but the opposite parties refused to receive the rent with ill motive and bad intention. Thereafter, they sent the said monthly rent to the opposite party by money order No.0514 dated 9-12-2004 which was returned back to the petitioner on 29-12-2004 and she also sent the rent for the month of December, 2004 by money order No.1674 dated 1-1-2005 which was also refused by the opposite party and returned back to the petitioner. Consequently, the petitioner deposited the rent for the month of November and December, 2004 before the rent controller by filing House Rent Case No.6 of 2005. 

 3. The opposite parties appeared in the case and contested the same by filing written objection contending inter alia, that the agreement in between the parties in respect of the premises already expired and the petitioner is an undesirable tenant and also stated that the premises in question has already been burned out by fire and there is no existence of the schedule premises and, as such, the question of the tenancy right and to receive any rent from the petitioner does not arise at all. Learned House Rent Controller rejected the case for default on 28-3-2006 as the petitioner failed to appear before the court on the date fixed. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order of the House Rent Controller the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.99 of 2006 before the District Judge, Dhaka. Eventually, the said appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka on transfer who upon hearing dismissed the appeal by impugned judgment and order dated 17-6-2008. Thereafter, the petitioner moved before this Court by filing a Civil Revision No.2529 of 2008 against the impugned judgment and order of the appellate court and obtained Rule and order of stay. 

 5. Subsequently, the said Rule was discharged for non-prosecution on 11-3-2013 on the prayer of the petitioner. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the House Rent Controller on 17-6-2013 seeking permission to withdraw the rent deposited with the controller. The learned Assistant Judge and the House Rent Controller, Dhaka heard the application and rejected the same by the impugned order dated 22-9-2013. The petitioner against the order of the House Rent Controller moved before the District Judge by filing a Civil Revision No.196 of 2013. Eventually, the said revision was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka on transfer who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and order dated 9-11-2014 rejected the same. 

 7. Mr Nakib Saiful Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the suit premises for which the petitioner deposited monthly rent with the rent controller is admittedly burned out by fire and there is no existence of premises physically as admitted by the opposite party by filing written objection before the House Rent Controller and, as such, the opposite parties are not at all entitled to get or receive any rent for a non existent premises. He further submits that the opposite parties unequivocally admitted that the suit premises already been burnt by fire and there is no existence of premises and, as such, the question of acceptance of rent for the non existent premises does not arise at ail, therefore, the rent deposited by the petitioner with the rent controller is liable to be refunded to the petitioner. Mr Nakib further submits that section 14 of the Premises Rent Control Act provided provision for refund of rent, premium, salami etc. not recoverable under the act. Since the rent deposited with the House Rent Controller are not recoverable by the opposite party from the petitioner on the ground of non existence of the premises, the petitioner is legally entitled to get refund of the amount deposited with the controller. But the trial court without assigning any reason in a very slipshod manner passed the order rejecting the application for refund of the money. He further goes to argue that the appellate court is a court under the act and can exercise all the powers as a civil court but though the petitioner filed a revision against the order of the House Rent Controller instead of filing an appeal the appellate court below ought to have observed that it has power and authority to pass a judicial order as court of appeal but rejected the revision only observing that the petitioner deposited the rent to be paid to the landlord. 

 8. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.1- 2 at the very outset submits that the House Rent Controller is not a court like a civil court. The controller is a mere conduit pipe it cannot decide any dispute between the land-lord and the tenant and the deposit of rent in the office of the controller is not an institution of a case as the controller upon such deposit does not decide the dispute between the parties, As such, the application filed by the petitioner under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not at all maintainable and the rent controller cannot pass any order accepting such application filed by the petitioner. He further submits that premises rent control act only provided provision for the tenant to deposit rent with the rent controller to be paid to the landlord and there is no provision allowing the tenant to withdraw the deposit made with the rent controller in favour of the landlord. As such, the prayer for withdrawal of the rent deposited with the rent controller by the petitioner was rightly rejected. He further submits that the order of the rent controller is appealable under section 30 of the Premises Rent Control Act, but the present petitioner instead of filing appeal filed civil revision before the District Judge which was not at all maintainable. 

 9. Mr Quyum further goes to argue that the petitioner has only way to file a civil suit for a declaration that the rent deposited with the rent controller are not payable to the opposite party and the petitioner is entitled to withdraw the same and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the case of Md. Osman vs Fatema Khatoon reported in 41 DLB 270 and Nurul Alam vs Dr. Shahjahan Howlader (Md) reported in 6 BLC 77. 

 10. Heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, have gone through the application under section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Act, 1991 filed by the petitioner before the rent controller for deposit of the monthly rent, written objection filed by the opposite parties before the rent controller and the impugned judgment and order of the courts below. 

 11. From perusal of application filed by the petitioner before the rent controller for withdrawal of money deposited as monthly rent, it appears that the petitioner deposited rent from the month of November, 2004 upto the month of February, 2013 in House Rent Case No.6 of 2005, Learned House Rent Controller rejected the case on 17-6-2008 for default; thereafter, the petitioner unsuccessfully moved upto the High Court Division and made the Rule discharged for non-prosecution on 11-3-2013. Thereafter, the petitioner filed application on 17-6-2013 before the rent controller praying for withdrawal of the money deposited with it favouring the opposite parties, Learned House Rent Controller rejected the application saying as follows: 

 12. The order passed by the House Rent Controller shows that it has stated no reason even a single word for rejection of the application filed by the petitioner, In disposing any application by the court below it must give some reason why the application is rejected. The revisional court below while rejecting the revision observed and held that: 

 13. The above observations of the revisional court shows that in passing the order the court only considered the petitioner as a tenant under the opposite party and observed that the amount so have been deposited with the rent controller in favour of the landlord for the premises under the occupation of the petitioner. Thereafter, as per terms and conditions of the agreement only the landlord is entitled to get the money deposited. But totally failed to appreciate the fact that the premises in question for which the rent was deposited with the rent controller has been totally destroyed by fire and the opposite parties also in their written statement at para 12(c) unequivocally admitted and stated that "the schedule premises has already been burned out by fire and there is no existence of the schedule premises and, as such, the question of tenancy right and to receive any rent from the petitioner does not arise at all". Because of clear admission of the opposite parties that the premises in question already burned out by fire and there is no existence of premises, in one hand they lost the status of landlord and on the other hand the petitioner is no more a tenant under them and the deposit was wrongly made by the petitioner on the wrong advise of her lawyer and, as such, the amount so deposited with the rent controller by the petitioner are liable to be refunded to the petitioner as the opposite parties are not at all entitled to receive the same from the date of burn out of the premises. 

 14. This Court agreed with the contention of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties that the rent controller is not a court and an application under section 151 of the Code is not entertainable by it but the premises rent control act empowered the House Rent Controller to make refund of the deposit to the petitioner which is not recoverable by the landlord. 

 15. From the facts and circumstances of the case it is seen that the money deposited with the rent controller are not at all recoverable from the petitioner by the opposite parties and, as such, the rent controller had authority or power to make necessary order for refund of the money deposited by the petitioner. It is also true that any order passed by the House Rent Controller is appealable under section 30 of the Premises Rent Control Act before the District Judge. But in the instant case the petitioner instead of preferring an appeal filed a revision against the order of the House Rent Controller. It is also a wrong done by the conducting lawyer of the petitioner and this point was not raised by the opposite parties before the revisional court. Consequently, the court below disposed of the revision on contest. However, the petitioner moved this Court under revisional jurisdiction rightly. The error whatever occurred before the District Judge for the reason of conducting lawyer is not so fatal and it has no substantial contribution in the merit of the case. 

 17. However, from the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court thinks that the hands of this Court are not so short and to do justice this Court can pass an order allowing withdrawal of the money deposited with the House Rent Controller by the petitioner as a court of law and in the event of allowing the petitioner to withdraw the money wrongly deposited with the House Rent Controller on the wrong advise of the learned Advocate justice will be done and there will be no injustice to the opposite parties, as they categorically admitted that there is no existence of premises for which they cannot receive rent from the petitioner. 

 18. Apart from this the opposite parties have not yet filed any application before the House Rent Controller praying for withdrawal of the money deposited by the petitioner in their favour claiming the amount as landlord as they know that they are not entitled to receive the same. In that view of the matter also opposite parties claim has become barred under the law. 

 19. This Court thinks that for the reason of absence of any provision in the act to withdraw any amount deposited with the House Rent Controller by the tenant, the petitioner is not required to file any independent civil suit before any court for declaration to the effect that they are entitled to receive or withdraw the money deposited with the rent controller as it would again put the petitioner into a further litigation unnecessarily. 

 22. Impugned judgment and order passed by the courts below are hereby set aside. The petitioner is hereby permitted to withdraw the money deposited with the Rent Controller and the House Rent Controller is hereby directed to pass necessary order for withdrawal of the money by the petitioner.
